dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: Good morning, Muhammad.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: Good morning, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: Good, but I'm still a bit sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: It's a quarter past seven.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: لَازِم أُطْلِع، عِنْدِي شُغْل السَّاعَة ثَمَانِيَة.
dialogue.english: I have to leave, I have work at eight.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: Do you want coffee before you leave?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: إِي، بَس بِسُرْعَة، مَا عِنْدِي وَقْت.
dialogue.english: Yes, but quickly, I don't have time.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: Here, drink and go to work.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: Thanks, see you in the evening.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: Bye, take care of yourself.

response.english: Yes, I woke up at six.

pair.english: Do you want coffee first thing?

response.arabic: إِي أَكِيد، مَا أَقْدِر بِدُون قَهْوَة
response.english: Yes of course, I can't do without coffee.

lessons.culture: In the Hejaz, mornings start with the greeting "صباح الخير" and a small cup of strong Arabic coffee is nearly universal before leaving home, even on a rushed morning. Family names are often used in greetings.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "صباح الخير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.item: صباح الخير عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته
too_formal.feedback: This greeting is correct but far more elaborate than the everyday morning reply.

exercises.tip: The fixed everyday reply to "صباح الخير" is "صباح النور".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "كم الساعة دحين؟" Answer that it's seven o'clock.

too_formal.feedback: This is a bookish way to say the time; nobody says it like this out loud.

exercises.tip: "الساعة + number" is the everyday pattern for telling time.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "أَبْغَى _____ عَلَى الرِّيق." English meaning: I want coffee first thing.

too_formal.feedback: This wording is more explicit and formal than the simple everyday word.

exercises.tip: "عَلَى الرِّيق" means before eating anything, right after waking up.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "الصُّبْح بِدْرِي الْبَرْد _____." English meaning: Early morning the cold is very.

too_formal.feedback: This phrasing is correct but reads like a written weather report, not spoken Hejazi.

exercises.tip: "مَرَّة" means "very/a lot" and is how the Hejaz intensifies adjectives.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Hejazi Arabic: "I woke up early."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Hejazi speech.

exercises.tip: "صِحِتْ" is the everyday Hejazi verb for "woke up".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I missed the bus."

too_formal.feedback: This is grammatical but far too formal for everyday complaining about a bus.

exercises.tip: "فَاتَنِي" is used for missing a bus, a train, or any chance that passed.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'm still sleepy."

too_formal.feedback: This is textbook Arabic; "لِسَّه" is the natural spoken word for "still".

exercises.tip: "لِسَّه" before an adjective is how "still ..." is said in Hejazi speech.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I left for work"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is written-style Arabic, not the spoken phrase being practiced.

exercises.tip: "طَلِعْتُ لِلشُّغْل" literally means "I went up/out for work".

exercises.prompt: Which reply fits "صباح الخير" best?

too_formal.feedback: Just repeating "صباح الخير" back sounds stiff; a real reply changes the word.

exercises.tip: "صَبَاح النُّور" and "صَبَاح الْوَرْد" are both natural replies to a morning greeting.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "بِدْرِي / لِلشُّغْل / طَلِعْتُ"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this word order and vocabulary belong to written Arabic.

exercises.tip: Verb, then place, then time is the natural spoken order here.

dialogue.speaker: نُور
dialogue.english: Hi Muhammad, you arrived early today.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: Yes, I have a meeting at ten.

dialogue.speaker: نُور
dialogue.english: Okay, will you have lunch with me later?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: أَكِيد، بَس لَازِم أَخَلِّص هَالشُّغْلَة قَبْل الظُّهْر.
dialogue.transliteration: akeed, bas laazim akhallis hash-shughla 2abl iZ-Zuhur.
dialogue.english: Sure, but I have to finish this task before noon.

dialogue.speaker: نُور
dialogue.english: Can you take a break now?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: No, I have a lot of work now.

dialogue.speaker: نُور
dialogue.arabic: تِمَام، رَح أَدُور عَلَيْك بَعِد الظُّهْر.
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll look for you in the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: زَيْن، رَح أَتَّصِل فِيك إِذَا خَلَّصْتُ بِدْرِي.
dialogue.transliteration: zayn, ra7 attaSil fiik iza khallast bdri.
dialogue.english: Great, I'll call you if I finish early.

dialogue.speaker: نُور
dialogue.english: Are you hungry now or later?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: A bit hungry, but I can wait.

dialogue.speaker: نُور
dialogue.arabic: تِمَام، شُوفِنِي عِنْد الْبَاب السَّاعَة وَاحِد.
dialogue.english: Okay, meet me at the door at one.

pair.english: Do you have a meeting now?

lessons.culture: In Hejazi offices, colleagues often gather for lunch together and tea breaks are common. Saying "تِعْبَان" (tired) openly is natural and not seen as complaining, and people use "رَح" for the future tense.

exercises.prompt: A coworker asks: "وين تتغدى؟" Reply that you eat at home.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine, but far too formal for answering a quick lunch question.

exercises.tip: "عِنْد الْبَيْت" is the short, natural answer for "at home".

exercises.prompt: A coworker asks: "أقدر آخذ استراحة؟" Say yes, go ahead.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but sounds like a written permission slip, not a quick spoken okay.

exercises.tip: "تَفَضَّل" alone is a very common way to say "go ahead".

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "عِنْدِي اجْتِمَاع السَّاعَة _____." English meaning: I have a meeting at ten.

too_formal.feedback: This is a correct but formal way of stating the hour, closer to a schedule than speech.

exercises.tip: Numbers for the hour are said plainly after "الساعة".

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "_____، أَبْغَى آكُل حَاجَة." English meaning: I'm hungry, I want to eat something.

too_formal.feedback: This describes hunger in a clinical, written way rather than the short spoken word.

exercises.tip: "جُوعَان" on its own is how hunger is announced in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Hejazi Arabic: "I have a lot of work now."

too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; "دِحِين" for "now" is the spoken word actually used.

exercises.tip: "دِحِين" means "now" in everyday Hejazi speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll call you in the afternoon."

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "رَح" instead of "سـ" is what marks it as spoken Hejazi.

exercises.tip: "رَح" before a verb is the everyday future marker.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I finished my work early today."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct written Arabic; "خَلَّصْتُ" and "بِدْرِي" are the spoken choices.

exercises.tip: "خَلَّصْتُ" is the everyday verb for "I finished".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I'm a bit tired now"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this reads like a written statement rather than spoken Hejazi.

exercises.tip: "شْوَيّ" softens an adjective to mean "a bit".

exercises.prompt: Which word completes: "أَدُور عَلَى _____." English meaning: I'm looking for my pen.

too_formal.feedback: Adding "الْخَاص" for "my own" is unnecessary and sounds overly formal here.

exercises.tip: "أَدُور عَلَى" means "I'm looking for" and is followed directly by the thing.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "بِدْرِي / وِصِلْتُ / لِلشُّغْل"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this vocabulary and order belong to written Arabic.

exercises.tip: Verb, then place, then time is the natural spoken order here too.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: I'm home, good evening.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: Good evening, how was your day?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: تِعِبْتُ مَرَّة الْيَوم، بَس خَلَّصْتُ كُلّ شُغْلِي.
dialogue.transliteration: ti3ibt marra il-yoom, bas khallast kull shughli.
dialogue.english: I got very tired today, but I finished all my work.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: أَيّ حَاجَة بَسِيطَة، بَس أَبْغَى أَسْتَحِمّ أَوَّل.
dialogue.transliteration: ayy 7aaja baSiTa, bas abgha astahi awwal.
dialogue.english: Anything simple, I want to shower first.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.arabic: تِمَام، خَلِّينَا نِطْلِع نِتْمَشَّى شْوَيّ بَعِد الْعِشَا.
dialogue.transliteration: tammam, khalina niTli3 nitmashsha shwayy ba3d il-3asha.
dialogue.english: Okay, let's go out for a little walk after dinner.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: Good idea, the weather is nice in the evening.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: Then do you want to watch a series?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: إِي، بَس رَح نِيم بِدْرِي اللَّيْلَة.
dialogue.transliteration: ee, bas ra7 niim bdri il-leela.
dialogue.english: Yes, but I'll sleep early tonight.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.arabic: تِمَام، أَبْغَى أَتَّصِل فِي أَهْلِي قَبْل مَا نِيم.
dialogue.transliteration: tammam, abgha attaSil fi ahli 2abl ma niim.
dialogue.english: Okay, I want to call my family before we sleep.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: Good night when you're done.

pair.english: Do you want to watch a series?

lessons.culture: "تِصْبَح عَلَى خَيْر" is answered with the fixed phrase "وَإِنْتَ مِنْ أَهْلُه", which does not translate word for word; evenings in the Hejaz are for family time, and many people spend the cool hours after sunset visiting neighbors or taking a short walk.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "مسا الخير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.feedback: Simply repeating the greeting back sounds stiff; a real reply changes the word.

exercises.tip: "مَسَا النُّور" is the fixed everyday reply to an evening greeting.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "تصبح على خير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.feedback: This is understandable but not the fixed idiom people actually use here.

exercises.tip: "وَإِنْتَ مِنْ أَهْلُه" is a set phrase; it does not translate literally.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "أَبْغَى _____، تِعِبْتُ مَرَّة الْيَوم." English meaning: I want to shower, I got very tired today.

too_formal.feedback: Adding "أَنْ" before the verb is grammatical but far too formal for a spoken plan.

exercises.tip: "أَبْغَى" is directly followed by the verb with no extra word in between.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "خَلِّينَا نِطْلِع _____ شْوَيّ." English meaning: Let's go out for a little walk.

too_formal.feedback: This is a formal, written way to describe walking rather than the everyday verb.

exercises.tip: "نِتْمَشَّى" is the everyday word for taking a walk.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Hejazi Arabic: "I came back home."

too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; "الْبَيْت" and "رَجَعْتُ" are the words used in speech.

exercises.tip: "الْبَيْت" is the everyday word for home.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll sleep early tonight."

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "رَح" and "بِدْرِي" are what mark it as spoken.

exercises.tip: "اللَّيْلَة" means "tonight", not "the night" in general.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The weather is nice in the evening."

too_formal.feedback: "الطَّقْس" is the formal written word for weather; "الْجَوّ" is what is said in speech.

exercises.tip: "الْجَوّ" is the everyday word for weather.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Good night"?

too_formal.feedback: This is a stiff, written-style wish rather than the everyday spoken phrase.

exercises.tip: "تِصْبَح عَلَى خَيْر" is said only when someone is about to sleep.

exercises.prompt: Which reply fits "كيف كان يومك؟" best?

too_formal.feedback: This sounds like a written report on the day rather than a casual spoken answer.

exercises.tip: A short mix of feeling and outcome is how this is usually answered.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "الْبَيْت / رَجَعْتُ"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this vocabulary belongs to written Arabic.

exercises.tip: Verb first, then place, is the natural spoken order.

phrases.arabic: الأِسْبُوع الْجَاي فِيه اجْتِمَاع يَوم التِّلَات
phrases.transliteration: il-isboo3 ij-jaay fih ijtimaa3 yom it-talaat

phrases.arabic: يَوم الأَرْبِعَا عِنْدِي شُغْل لَحِد الْمَسَا
عِنْدِي شُغْل كُلّ يَوم غَيْر الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت
phrases.transliteration: 3indi shughel kull yoom gheer ij-jum3a wis-sabt

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: بَعِدِني مَا قَرَّرْتُ، لَيِش، عِنْدِك فِكْرَة؟
dialogue.english: I haven't decided yet, why, do you have an idea?

dialogue.speaker: نُور
dialogue.arabic: يَوم السَّبْت نِرُوح السُّوق، تِبْغَى تِجِي؟
dialogue.transliteration: yom is-sabt niruuh is-soo2, tibgha tiji?
dialogue.english: On Saturday we're going to the market, do you want to come?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: أَكِيد، بَس يَوم الْجُمْعَة عِنْدِي شُغْل شْوَيّ.
dialogue.transliteration: akeed, bas yom ij-jum3a 3indi shughel shwayy.
dialogue.english: Sure, but Friday I have a little work.

dialogue.speaker: نُور
dialogue.english: Isn't Friday a day off for you?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: عَادَة إِي، بَس هَالأِسْبُوع فِيه اجْتِمَاع يَوم التِّلَات وَبَعِدُه لَازِم أَخَلِّص شُغْلَة.
dialogue.transliteration: 3aada ee, bas hal-isboo3 fih ijtimaa3 yom it-talaat w ba3do laazim akhallis shughla.
dialogue.english: Usually yes, but this week there's a meeting on Tuesday and after it I have to finish a task.

dialogue.speaker: نُور
dialogue.english: Okay, when exactly is the meeting?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: Tuesday at ten o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: نُور
dialogue.arabic: تِمَام، يَوم الْخَمِيس بِشُوف رُفَايِقِي، بَعِدَيْن الْجُمْعَة بِصْلِي وَبِيرْتَاح.
dialogue.transliteration: tammam, yom il-khamis bishuuf rufaa2i, ba3dayn ij-jum3a biSalli w biyrtaa7.
dialogue.english: Okay, Thursday I see my friends, then Friday I pray and rest.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: كُلّ يَوم عِنْدِي شُغْل غَيْر الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت.
dialogue.transliteration: kull yoom 3indi shughel gheer ij-jum3a wis-sabt.
dialogue.english: I have work every day except Friday and Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: نُور
dialogue.arabic: نِهَايَة الأِسْبُوع تِيجِي بِسُرْعَة، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه.
dialogue.english: The weekend comes quickly, thank God.

pair.english: What do you plan to do on the weekend?

response.english: We're going to the market on Saturday.
No, Friday is a day off.

lessons.culture: The Hejazi work week typically runs Sunday through Thursday, with Friday kept for prayer and rest and Saturday often used for errands or the market. The phrase "إِيشْ يَوْم" (which day) is very common in Hejazi speech.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "إيش يوم الاجتماع؟" Say it's on Tuesday.

too_formal.feedback: This sounds like an official announcement, not a quick spoken answer.

exercises.tip: "يَوم + day name" is the everyday way to answer "when".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "الْيَوم شُو يَوم؟" Say today is Sunday.

too_formal.feedback: Adding "هُو" here is grammatical but sounds more like writing than speech.

exercises.tip: "الْيَوم يَوم + day" needs no linking word in spoken Hejazi.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "بُكْرَة يَوم _____." English meaning: Tomorrow is Monday.

too_formal.feedback: This is the correct written spelling but not how it is pronounced in Hejazi speech.

exercises.tip: "الاثْنَيْن" is how "Monday" is said out loud in the Hejaz.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "يَوم السَّبْت _____ السُّوق." English meaning: On Saturday we go to the market.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct written Arabic but drops the everyday "نِرُوح" spoken shape.

exercises.tip: "نِرُوح" is the "we" form of "go" in Hejazi speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Hejazi Arabic: "Friday is the day of prayer and rest."

too_formal.item: يَوم الْجُمْعَة هُو يَوم لِلصَّلَاة وَالرَّاحَة
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but the extra linking words make this sound like a written sentence.

exercises.tip: "الْجُمْعَة يَوم + X" needs no linking word in speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I have work every day except Friday and Saturday."
exercises.answer: عِنْدِي شُغْل كُلّ يَوم غَيْر الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت
accepted: عِنْدِي شُغْل كُلّ يَوم غَيْر الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت
شُغْل كُلّ يَوم إِلَّا الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت
عِنْدِي شُغْل كُلّ يَوم إِلَّا الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت

too_formal.item: لَدَيَّ عَمَل كُلّ يَوم مَا عَدَا الْجُمْعَة وَالسَّبْت
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is written style; "غَيْر" is the everyday word for "except".

exercises.tip: "غَيْر" before the excluded days is the spoken way to say "except".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The weekend comes quickly."

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this reads like a written sentence rather than something said out loud.

exercises.tip: "تِيجِي" is the everyday verb form for "it comes".

exercises.prompt: Which word means "Thursday"?

too_formal.feedback: Adding a description like "الْمُبَارَك" is unnecessary and overly formal for naming a day.

exercises.tip: "الْخَمِيس" on its own already means "Thursday".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "What do you plan to do on the weekend?"

too_formal.item: مَاذَا تَنْوِي أَنْ تَفْعَل فِي عُطْلَة نِهَايَة الأِسْبُوع؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but the extra linking word "أَنْ" makes this sound like writing.

exercises.tip: "نَاوِي" directly before the verb is how spoken Hejazi states an intention.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "الأَحَد / يَوم / الْيَوم"

too_formal.feedback: Grammatical, but the linking word "هُو" is dropped in ordinary spoken Hejazi.

exercises.tip: "الْيَوم يَوم + day name" needs no extra linking word.

challenge.title: Plan Your Week in Hejazi
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short conversation about a day and the week ahead, at least 10 lines. It must include a morning greeting and its reply, a question about the time, a statement about being tired or sleepy, an evening greeting and its reply, the good-night exchange, a question about a day of the week or a meeting time, and a plan for the weekend. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 7.
required_elements: A morning greeting using صباح الخير and its reply صباح النور.
A statement about waking up or being sleepy, using صحيت بدري or لسه نعسان.
A question using كم الساعة دحين؟ and a time answer.
A statement about being tired or having a lot of work, using تعبت or عندي شغل كتير.
An evening greeting using مسا الخير and its reply مسا النور.
The good-night exchange using تصبح على خير and وإنت من أهله.
A question using إيش يوم or كم السّاعة and its answer.
A statement naming at least two days of the week.
A plan for the weekend using نهاية الأسبوع.
At least one invitation or suggestion, such as تبغى تجي؟ or خلينا نطلع.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: Good morning, how are you today?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: صَبَاح النُّور، تِمَام، بَس لِسَّه نَعْسَان شْوَيّ.
dialogue.transliteration: sabaa7 in-noor, tammam, bas lissa na3saan shwayy.
dialogue.english: Good morning, good, but still a bit sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: What time is it now?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: السَّاعَة سَبْعَة، لَازِم أُطْلِع لِلشُّغْل بِسُرْعَة.
dialogue.transliteration: is-saa3a sab3a, laazim uTli3 lish-shughel bsur3a.
dialogue.english: It's seven, I have to leave for work quickly.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: Okay, when will you be back?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: بَعِد الظُّهْر، عِنْدِي شُغْل كِتِير دِحِين.
dialogue.english: In the afternoon, I have a lot of work now.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: Good evening, I got very tired today.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.arabic: مَسَا النُّور، خَلِّينَا نِطْلِع نِتْمَشَّى شْوَيّ.
dialogue.transliteration: masa in-noor, khalina niTli3 nitmashsha shwayy.
dialogue.english: Good evening, let's go out for a little walk.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: فِكْرَة حِلْوَة، بَس أَبْغَى أَسْتَحِمّ أَوَّل.
dialogue.english: Good idea, but I want to shower first.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.arabic: تِمَام، شُو نَاوِي تِعْمَل نِهَايَة الأِسْبُوع؟
dialogue.transliteration: tammam, shoo nawi ti3mal nihayat il-isboo3?
dialogue.english: Great, what do you plan to do on the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: يَوم الْخَمِيس بِشُوف رُفَايِقِي، وَيَوم السَّبْت نِرُوح السُّوق.
dialogue.transliteration: yom il-khamis bishuuf rufaa2i, w yom is-sabt niruuh is-soo2.
dialogue.english: On Thursday I see my friends, and on Saturday we go to the market.

dialogue.speaker: فَاطِمَة
dialogue.english: Good night, see you tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: You too.
